subsystems.name: Cell source
subsystems.role: provides the starting cells that self-organise into tissue.

subsystems.name: Matrix and scaffold
subsystems.role: mimics the extracellular environment that supports three-dimensional growth.

subsystems.name: Differentiation cues
subsystems.role: chemical signals that steer stem cells into specific tissue types.

subsystems.name: Bioreactor and perfusion
subsystems.role: supplies nutrients and removes waste as the organoid grows.

subsystems.name: Sensing and readouts
subsystems.role: measures how the organoid responds to drugs or disease.

subsystems.name: Vascular and immune components
subsystems.role: optional additions that make organoids more realistic.

buildSteps.title: Source the cells
buildSteps.detail: Take a small tissue biopsy or reprogram adult cells, such as skin or blood, into induced pluripotent stem cells.

buildSteps.title: Expand and quality-check
buildSteps.detail: Grow the stem cells in culture and confirm they are pluripotent and genetically stable.

buildSteps.title: Embed in matrix
buildSteps.detail: Mix a defined number of cells with extracellular matrix gel and deposit them as droplets in a culture plate.

buildSteps.title: Guide differentiation
buildSteps.detail: Add growth factors and inhibitors in a precise sequence over days to weeks to form the desired tissue, such as kidney, brain or gut.

buildSteps.title: Mature the organoid
buildSteps.detail: Culture for weeks to months, changing media and sometimes applying flow, until the organoid develops structured layers up to about 1 mm thick.

buildSteps.title: Add vasculature or immune cells
buildSteps.detail: Co-culture with endothelial cells to form vessel-like channels, or with immune cells to model inflammation; bioprinting can assemble larger structures.

buildSteps.title: Characterise and validate
buildSteps.detail: Use microscopy, sequencing and functional tests to confirm the organoid matches the target tissue and is reproducible.

buildSteps.title: Apply in testing or therapy
buildSteps.detail: Expose the organoid to drug candidates, or use patient-derived organoids to predict which treatment will work for that patient.

pathway.milestone: organoids used in academic research and preclinical drug screening
pathway.unlocks: better prediction of drug toxicity and efficacy before animal tests.

pathway.milestone: patient-derived organoids in clinical trials to guide cancer therapy
pathway.unlocks: personalised treatment selection, especially for cancers.
